readerTitle: Why the better product often loses
caseNote: 가상 사례 (배관공, 가사 청소 서비스, 물류용 플라스틱 상자 제조사) · 마케팅의 표준 개념(고려 집합) 인용
insight: 고객은 존재하는 것 중 가장 좋은 것이 아니라 자기 눈앞에 보이는 것 중 가장 좋은 것을 고른다. 그래서 경쟁의 상당 부분은 품질 비교 전에, 고객의 짧은 후보 목록에 오르는 단계에서 끝난다.
misconception: 제품이 충분히 좋으면 고객은 알아서 찾아온다. 그러니 남는 예산은 품질을 더 높이는 데 써야 한다.

sources.text: Howard, J. A. & Sheth, J. N. (1969). The Theory of Buyer Behavior. (고려 집합 'evoked/consideration set' 개념의 고전적 출처)
모든 사례와 수치는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 고려 집합(consideration set) 개념의 출처로 Howard & Sheth(1969)를 적었습니다. 이 책에서는 'evoked set'이라는 용어를 썼습니다. 카드에는 특정 연구 수치를 쓰지 않고 개념만 설명했습니다. 출처 표기가 적절한지 게시 전 확인하세요.
청소 서비스 사례의 '두 배 많은 예약', '15% 가격 인하'는 모두 설명용 가상 수치입니다.
대형 물류·창고 운영사가 승인 공급업체 목록(approved vendor list)을 통해 구매한다는 설정은 일반적인 B2B 구매 관행을 단순화한 가상 사례입니다.

cards.title: Why the better product often loses
body: A pipe bursts under the sink at 10 p.m. Water is spreading across the floor. You don't research the best plumber in town. You call the number on the magnet stuck to your fridge.
That plumber may be only the third-best in town. Tonight, it doesn't matter. The best plumber never got the call.

image.label: A plumber's fridge magnet beside a leaking kitchen sink
image.brief: 밤의 부엌. 싱크대 아래로 물이 번지고, 사람이 냉장고에 붙은 배관공 자석 광고를 보며 전화를 걸고 있음. 자석에는 가상의 이름과 번호만, 실제 상호나 로고는 쓰지 않음. 따뜻한 일러스트 스타일.

cards.title: Better reviews, fewer bookings.
body: You run a house-cleaning service. Your reviews are the best in your area, and customers who try you tend to stay. A rival with average reviews still books about twice as many homes.
You have a small budget for next quarter. Where does it go?

options.text: Train staff further and switch to premium eco-friendly products
options.feedback: Your quality lead is already real. Making it bigger doesn't reach the people who have never heard of you.

options.text: Get recommended by local property managers and real-estate agents
options.feedback: This puts your name in front of people at the moment they choose a cleaner. You spend less on quality, but quality wasn't the gap.

options.text: Cut prices 15% to win customers from the rival
options.feedback: A lower price helps once people compare you. But they still have to find you first, and you'd keep less on every job.

cards.title: A contest you were never entered in.
body: The rival's owner spent years building ties with property managers. Every new tenant got a welcome pack with her number in it.
People who have just moved need a cleaner fast, and they rarely shop around. They used the name they were handed. Many never compared her service with yours at all.
Your better service didn't lose on quality. It lost before quality was ever judged.

cards.title: Distribution beats product
body: **Distribution** is how your product reaches customers at the moment they decide to buy: where they see it, who recommends it, and how easy it is to get.
Customers don't choose the best option that exists. They choose the best option they *see*. A better product missing from that view loses to a good-enough one that's right there.

image.label: A large hidden gem behind a wall versus a small stone in plain view
image.brief: 인포그래픽. 왼쪽: 담장 뒤에 숨은 크고 빛나는 보석 "Better product". 오른쪽: 길가에 바로 보이는 평범한 돌 "Good-enough product". 지나가는 고객이 오른쪽 돌을 집어 드는 장면. 담장에는 "Not seen" 라벨.

cards.title: The short list in the customer's head.
body: Marketers call it the **consideration set**: the few options a customer actually weighs. It is usually small, and it forms before the decision, from what is nearby, familiar or recommended.
So much of the competition happens in getting onto that list. Once you're on it, quality starts to count. Until then, it barely counts at all.

cards.title: The same pattern, in every industry.
body: Look for the moment a buyer meets a few options:
list: A snack at eye level on the supermarket shelf
A supplier already on a company's approved list
The lawyer your accountant happens to mention
The first results for "plumber near me"
cards.callout: In each case, the winner was picked from the options in view, not from the whole market.
cards.softwareNote: In software, a better tool often loses to one that comes bundled with something customers already use, or is set as the default. Many users never go looking for an alternative.

cards.title: Distribution gets you tried. Product gets you kept.
body: Reach without quality backfires. More people try you, more of them leave, and more of them warn others. Strong distribution makes a weak product fail faster.
Reach also costs money. Partners, shelf space and ads all take a share. The lesson isn't to ignore the product. It's to stop assuming a better product will find its own customers.

image.label: A funnel: many people enter, a leaky bucket loses them
image.brief: 깔때기 위로 많은 사람이 들어오고("Distribution"), 아래 양동이("Product")에 구멍이 나 있어 사람들이 새어 나가는 그림. 양동이 옆에 "Keeps customers" 라벨.

cards.title: Now it's a crate factory.
body: Your factory makes plastic shipping crates for warehouses. Yours are lighter and last longer than the market leader's.
But large warehouse operators buy only from suppliers on an approved vendor list, and you're not on most of them. Where does next year's effort go?

options.text: Design an even lighter crate to make the gap obvious
options.feedback: You'd widen a lead that buyers can't see. The purchasing team still orders from its list, and you're still not on it.

options.text: Go through the vendor approval process at three large operators
options.feedback: It's slow, paperwork-heavy work. But it puts you on the list buyers actually choose from, so your better crate finally gets compared.

options.text: Run online ads aimed at warehouse staff who handle crates
options.feedback: Staff may love your crate, but they usually don't place the order. Ads build awareness without getting you onto the list purchasing uses.

cards.title: A better product only wins among the options customers see.
body: Before improving what you sell, ask whether customers meet it when they're ready to buy.
**Try it today:** ask your last five customers how they found you and who else they considered. Then list the places where people decide to buy but you don't appear.
